newsitem.title: USA: John Morrell Sioux Falls pork plant cutting shift.
newsitem.headline: John Morrell Sioux Falls pork plant cutting shift.

text.p: John Morrell and Co's hog slaughter plant in Sioux Falls, S.D. will suspend second shift operations for one week starting Monday, a company spokesman said.
"Hog numbers are not out there right now," said Jeff Luckman, vice president of hog procurement at Smithfield Foods Inc which owns John Morrell and Co.
"We also have maintenance to do and it will only be for a week," Luckman added.
About 600 workers will be affected by the temporary shift closure, sources close to the company said.
The Sioux Falls plant typically runs two shifts and has a daily slaughter capacity of 15,000 head, industry sources said.

Morrell's two hog plants in Sioux Falls S.D. and Sioux City, Iowa have not been operating at full capacity since May 5. They, along with many major hog plants, trimmed output several weeks ago when operating margins plummeted on high hog prices and sluggish pork demand, industry and company sources said.
The second shift at Morrell's Sioux City plant was cut indefinitely in early February in an attempt to mend margins, a company source said then.

Smithfield operates a hog plant in Tar Heel, N.C., with a daily capacity of about 24,000 head and a plant in Smithfield Va., with a capacity of about 10,000, industry sources said. Another Smithfield subsidiary, Gwaltney of Smithfield Ltd, has a hog plant in Gwaltney, Va., with estimated capacity of 9,000 head, the sources said.
